correctness.rationale: Conant–Kruckman, Prop. 2.14 and Cor. 2.15, identify complete types with marked join/meet closures. The Fano plane is a finite K_{2,2}-free incidence structure and embeds into a model of T_{2,2} by the model-companion theorem; its joins and meets already exist in it, so its marked tuples retain their closures. This supplies witnesses, not just combinatorial upper bounds. Completeness gives S_0=1; there are two one-element sorts, and the pair census is 2 equal + 2 distinct same-sort + 4 oriented mixed = 8. Triples with repetitions give 2+3*6=20. An injective same-sort triple gives two possibilities per sort: one join/meet if collinear/concurrent, or three if not; the latter are pairwise incident to the marked elements as a triangle and yield no further closure. In a mixed triple the two same-sort elements generate one line or point; if that new element is distinct from the marked opposite-sort element, one meet/join of those two suffices, and no further elements are forced. Thus each of the six ordered mixed sort patterns has four marked incidence patterns of closure sizes 3,4,4,5; the four same-sort types add two of size 4 and two of size 6. Total 28 injective, 48 in all, with the stated histogram. Theorem 3.3 constructs 2^aleph0 distinct 4-types; coordinate repetition and countability give equality at all n>=4. `python /workspace/audit_checks_1_5.py 4` independently enumerates Fano signatures with closure growth, obtaining 1,2,8,48 and 6,14,6,2. It does not prove the type/closure theorem or the continuum bound.

evidence: Theorem 2.8 supplies the model companion; Prop. 2.14 and Cor. 2.15 give a general criterion on closures. Remark 3.4(3) states that closures generated by at most three elements are finite and that four is the first infinite arity. The proof of Theorem 3.3 actually gives the full continuum lower bound at arity four.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These statements cover the high-arity spectrum and the low-arity finiteness threshold, but give neither the finite numbers nor the decomposition by closure size. The exact low-arity classification must control which joins and meets coincide, which incidences are forced, and which marked diagrams are realizable.

value.rationale: This exactly resolves the finite side of the already motivated type-space threshold in a standard test theory. The full injective histogram supplies the possible local algebraic closures and their marked multiplicities before the continuum jump, usable in low-arity type analysis. It is a complete classification requiring exhaustion and realizability, not a computation of isolated examples or the already known arity-four result.
